title: Vendela Health POC - language selection, sizing & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping for a clinical summarization and triage pilot; primary asks: multilingual support (EN/ES/FR/SE), strict PHI handling (HIPAA), latency SLO ~300-500ms for short summaries, throughput planning for 50-100 concurrent editors. Next steps: share benchmark harness, security packet, schedule on-prem networking sync, run initial 3-model micro-bench next week.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sara L. (Vendela Head ML), Arjun P. (Vendela Platform), Miriam O. (Clinical), Tom W. (PM)

[00:00] Olivia: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — im olivia, AE on inference, mateo and priya from the se side. how are you all?
[00:12] Sara: doing well, thanks. want to make sure we cover multilingual and PHI constraints early.
[00:18] Mateo: great, we have an agenda — scoping success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist models and tradeoffs, then benchmarks & timeline.
[00:28] Tom: sounds good. we have 2 goals: 1) automate visit summaries for triage, 2) extract structured fields for downstream analytics.
[00:36] Priya: and is that across languages? i remember spanish and french plus some nordic tests?
[00:42] Sara: yes english and spanish primary, french for pilot, and a small swedish set flagged by ops.
[00:48] Arjun: from infra side — we need to validate VPC options, KMS for keys, and ensure no raw PHI leaves our cloud buckets.
[01:02] Olivia: noted. from a success metrics POV what does clinical quality look like? miriam?
[01:08] Miriam: for summaries we want >= 85% correctness on key findings (vital complaints, diagnosis hints), <5% hallucination in red-lines, and structured extraction F1 > 0.82. those are ballpark.
[01:22] Mateo: perfect. on latency and throughput — what does client UX need? tom?
[01:27] Tom: editors want near-instant for short notes, ideally 300-500ms P95 for 200-300 token summaries; batch jobs can be higher. concurrency: editor team peaks ~50 concurrent, background ingest might be another 100 reqs/min.
[01:42] Mateo: ok so we should size both low-latency replica footprints and a separate batch path. cost matters — dedicated GPU for the pilot vs hosted?
[01:51] Sara: security-first. if dedicated reduces exposure and matches costs, we prefer dedicated but must see numbers.
[01:58] Olivia: for model shortlist we suggested only open models for this POC to avoid licensing friction: Llama 2 70B chat (hosted/dedicated), Llama 2 13B quantized, Mistral-30B, and Mistral-7B-Instruct for a lighter-weight option. we can also include a tuned Llama 2-13B q4f32 as a cost-performance baseline.
[02:20] Arjun: quick question — is falcon in scope?
[02:23] Mateo: we can add Falcon but performance varies by deployment; for medical summarization we have stronger signals on Llama2 and Mistral families.
[02:32] Miriam: how do we judge hallucination? what tests?
[02:35] Priya: our bench uses a mix: ROUGE for overlap, clinical QA (answering target questions), and explicit hallucination probes (fact-check prompts). we'll measure factuality and a human-in-the-loop sample review.
[02:48] Tom: will human review be blinded?
[02:51] Mateo: yes, recommended: clinical annotators blind to model identity for the first pass.
[02:57] Sara: about multilingual — do these models keep parity in Spanish and French? we do have limited in-domain Spanish terms, code mixing sometimes.
[03:05] Mateo: Llama2-70B tends to hold up best cross-lingually; Mistral-30B is competitive in English and decent in Spanish after instruction tuning, but we should expect a quality delta. Mistral-7B-Instruct might be noticeably weaker on complex clinical phrasing. quantized 13B models can be surprisingly good and much cheaper, but watch hallucination rate.
[03:29] Olivia: ok tradeoff summary: 70B = best quality, highest cost; 30B = balance; 13B-quant = best cost but monitoring for hallucination.
[03:39] Miriam: for patient safety we can't accept >5% hallucination; is that realistic with 13B?
[03:45] Priya: depends on prompts and post-processing; we also recommend a reranker / verifier step (lightweight QA model or rule-based checks) as a safety net. Redwood Optimize can run rerankers as an extra stage.
[03:58] Arjun: network/hosting — if we go private, will Redwood provide a private control plane and we host on our VPC?
[04:05] Olivia: yes, Redwood Private offers a control plane with customer-managed VPC. we integrate KMS for key management and can provide audit logs; we'll share SOC2 and architecture docs in the security packet.
[04:18] Tom: timeline?
[04:20] Olivia: proposal: week1 run micro-bench of 3 models (13B q4, mistral-7b-instruct, mistral-30b) with your sample de-id notes, capture latency, P95, and QA accuracy. week2 run multilingual QA and hallucination probes. week3-4 expand to Llama-70B candidate if needed while we finalize infra. pilot run 6 weeks with dedicated nodes and live validation. overall ~8-10 weeks from kickoff to pilot completion.
[04:47] Sara: that sounds workable. can you give an estimate cost range for dedicated nodes?
[04:52] Olivia: we'll attach a pricing estimate — rough numbers now: 13B quant dedicated pool for our expected concurrency ~ $Xk/month, 30B ~ $Yk/month, 70B much higher; we'll give a tiered quote.
[05:04] Arjun: we need a checklist for compliance signoff (SOC2, encryption, logs).
[05:08] Olivia: yes, sending security packet + SOC2 report and a checklist.
[05:12] Tom: on benchmarks: what ingestion pattern should we simulate?
[05:16] Mateo: please provide sample throughput distribution (p50 doc length, tokens per call, percent realtime vs batch). we'll simulate peak concurrency with our harness.
[05:25] Sara: we'll include a tagged dataset: 200 notes EN, 100 ES, 50 FR, 20 SE. that's de-identified.
[05:32] Olivia: perfect. for the micro-bench we'll do: latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, QA exact match, ROUGE-L, hallucination rate, and percentile cost per 1k summaries.
[05:43] Miriam: also include a manual spot-check of 50 summaries for clinical fidelity.
[05:47] Priya: agreed. that will help calibrate the automated metrics.
[05:52] Tom: any blockers we should address now?
[05:55] Arjun: firewall rules and peering — we'll need precise IPs and ports from Redwood.
[06:01] Olivia: we'll provide those in the network readiness doc.
[06:05] Sara: ok, recap and next steps?
[06:08] Olivia: recap: Redwood to share harness + readme (by 2/24), run micro-bench on our side with shared sample set, SEs to run initial runs (mateo), security packet to Vendela, schedule infra sync.
[06:21] Tom: schedule the infra sync — arjun and mateo coordinate.
[06:25] Mateo: i'll propose times.
[06:27] Miriam: if pilot goes well we'll push to dedicated for production.
[06:30] Olivia: great. any final questions?
[06:32] Sara: none from me. thanks everyone.
[06:35] Olivia: thanks — we'll follow up with notes and links. bye.

End of transcript. Note: rough automatic captions; some names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed.
